content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Platform Types and Java Nullability** as part of **Null Safety and Type Handling**. Kotlin distinguishes nullable types such as `String?` from non-null types such as `String`; callers must handle the nullable case explicitly. Use the subtopics—Understanding Platform Types, Java Interoperability Risks, Nullability Annotations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

content_blocks.text: Kotlin distinguishes nullable types such as `String?` from non-null types such as `String`; callers must handle the nullable case explicitly.

items.title: Nullability Annotations
items.text: Nullability Annotations is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.

content_blocks.text: The compiler can guarantee that a Java platform value never contains null.
